inclusion_criteria: Male and female patients listed to undergo orthognathic operations were sequentially invited to participate in the study.
exclusion_criteria: Use of antibiotics in the month before the operation, lactose intolerance (as the placebo was lactose-based) and patients who had previous orthognathic operations.

inclusion_criteria: Patients selected for participation in the study were healthy males and females presenting to the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Service at the Montreal General Hospital who were to undergo intraoral or combined intraoral and extraoral orthognathic surgical procedures, including those requiring autogenous bone grafts.

Patients presenting to Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, College of Dental Surgery, Saveetha University, Chennai, India, between September 2005 and December 2007 who were to undergo orthognathic surgery.
exclusion_criteria: 1) if patient had received an antibiotics 1 month before surgery; 2) if patient has history of allergy to ampicillin; 3) if any signs of active infection were present; 4) if the patient is immunocompromised.

Patients were excluded from the present study if they met the following criteria. 1) If patients presented with metabolic diseases or low resistance to infection. 2) If the patients needed a bone graft for the correction of dentofacial deformity. 3) If the patients sustained perioperative complications that make antibiotic usage more crucial, such as unfavorable fractures or excessive bleeding that can cause a large hematoma. 4) If the patients had received an antibiotic within 4 weeks of surgery. 5) If the patients had been treated by a distraction osteogenesis device or surgically assisted rapid palatal expansion. And, 6) If the patients had a history of allergy to penicillin.

Forty consecutive patients scheduled to undergo intraoral orthognathic surgery were chosen as subjects.
exclusion_criteria: Criteria for exclusion from the study included a history of allergy to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics, a compromised immune defense, and a history of having received antibiotic therapy within 14 days before the planned surgery.

inclusion_criteria: Fifty-six patients in their 20s without a specific medical history, and who were to undergo orthognathic surgical procedures at the department of oral and maxillofacial surgery at the dental hospital of Yonsei University were enrolled in this study.

70 consecutive patients who underwent a bilateral sagittal ramus osteotomy of the mandible. All patients were Angle Class II retrognathia patients, and all had preoperative orthodontic treatment to optimize the shape of the dental arches.
exclusion_criteria: (1) if they had received antibiotics within 2 weeks prior to surgery; (2) if a history of allergy to clindamycin existed; (3) if signs and symptoms of active infection were present; (4) if more surgical procedures (ie, chin or maxillary osteotomies) were indicated; or (5) if they suffered from severe underlying illness associated with compromised host defenses.

Exclusion criteria were a history of allergy to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics, any chronic medication use, use of antibiotics in the 4 weeks preceding admission, and a serum creatinine exceeding 110 mmol/L as an indication of the renal dysfunction.

inclusion_criteria: All patients, male and female, aged 18–40 years, who underwent bimaxillary orthognathic surgery within the Discipline of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery from December 2008 to May 2010, were enrolled in this study.
exclusion_criteria: history of any type of previous surgery to the head and neck area, including previous orthognathic surgery; patients who were having distraction osteogenesis as part of the orthognathic surgery; history of malignancy of the head and neck region, and/or history of radiation to the head and neck region; known hypersensitivity to amoxicillin, ampicillin or other β-lactam antibiotics; known history of lactose intolerance; patients who had used any antibiotics in the 14 days prior to the surgery; patients with compromised host defences (e.g. diabetes mellitus, autoimmune disease, end-stage renal disease, severe alcoholic cirrhosis and neutropenia); and patients who were receiving immunosuppressive drugs that interfere with host defences (e.g. cyclosporine, steroids and cancer chemotherapeutic agents).
